_meta.description: Report vocabulary translated for a family. Each entry gives the plain rendering that carries the SAME meaning — not a simplification that loses one. Used by scripts/plain_language.py and by render_brief.py's family-register check.

how_to_read.plain: What to write instead. Replaces the term; it is not a gloss to put beside it.
how_to_read.keep: Terms the family must be able to say themselves — gene symbol, syndrome name, the test's name. Keep these and explain once.
how_to_read.careful: Where a careless translation changes the meaning. Read before rewriting.

_meta.the_rule: The fix for a technical term is deletion, not definition. If a plain sentence carries the meaning, write that sentence — do not write the term and then explain it.

de novo.plain: this change was not inherited from either parent — it happened for the first time in your child
de novo.careful: Do not shorten to 'new' or 'random'. Families hear 'random' as 'nobody's fault, but also nobody knows anything', and it is neither.

heterozygous.plain: the change is in one of the two copies of this gene
heterozygous.careful: Only mention copies at all if it matters for what happens next. Often it does not, and the sentence can simply go.

homozygous.plain: the change is in both copies of this gene

hemizygous.plain: there is only one copy of this gene, so there is no second copy to compensate
hemizygous.careful: Usually X-linked. Do not go into inheritance patterns unless asked — route that to genetic counselling.

mosaic.plain: the change is present in some of the body's cells but not all of them
mosaic.careful: Never imply that a lower percentage means a milder condition. The level in a blood sample does not predict the level elsewhere.

pathogenic.plain: the laboratory is confident this change is the cause
pathogenic.careful: Do not soften to 'may be the cause'. That is the *likely pathogenic* or VUS wording, and the difference is the whole point of the classification.

likely pathogenic.plain: the laboratory thinks this change is very probably the cause, though not with complete certainty
likely pathogenic.careful: Must keep the uncertainty. Rendering it as 'is the cause' promotes the finding a level.

variant of uncertain significance.plain: the laboratory found a change but there is not yet enough evidence to say whether it is related to your child's development, or is simply part of normal human variation
variant of uncertain significance.careful: The single most misread term in genetics. Not 'probably bad', not 'nothing'. Read references/vus_communication.md before writing about one.

benign.plain: this change is a normal variation and is not the cause

likely benign.plain: this change is very probably normal variation rather than the cause

variant.careful: 'Mutation' is the word families expect but it carries dread. 'Change' does the same work.

missense.plain: one building block of the gene is altered

nonsense.plain: the gene's instructions stop early, so the protein is not finished

frameshift.plain: the gene's instructions are shifted out of step from that point on

truncating.plain: the gene's instructions are cut short

loss-of-function.plain: this change stops the gene working as it should
loss-of-function.careful: For SCN2A, SCN8A and GRIN2A/2B the direction of effect decides treatment and cannot be read off the notation. Do not state it unless the report does.

gain-of-function.plain: this change makes the gene overactive

haploinsufficiency.plain: one working copy of this gene is not enough on its own

penetrance.plain: not everyone with this change is affected in the same way, or at all
penetrance.careful: Do not attach a percentage unless you retrieved one this session.

proband.plain: the person who was tested first — here, your child

segregation.plain: testing parents to see whether they carry the same change

cascade testing.plain: offering testing to other family members

carrier.plain: someone who has the change but is not affected by it themselves
carrier.careful: Carrier status has implications for relatives. Route to genetic counselling rather than elaborating.

copy number variant.plain: a missing or extra piece of a chromosome

duplication.plain: an extra copy of a piece

microarray.plain: a test that looks for missing or extra pieces of chromosome
microarray.careful: Worth keeping the name so they can recognise it on paperwork. Say what it could not look for.

exome sequencing.plain: a test that reads the parts of the genes where most changes are found

genome sequencing.plain: a test that reads almost all of the DNA

gene panel.plain: a test that reads a fixed list of genes chosen in advance

repeat expansion.plain: a short piece of DNA repeated more times than usual

methylation.plain: a chemical marker that switches a gene on or off

transcript.plain: the specific version of the gene the laboratory measured against
transcript.careful: Rarely belongs in the family half at all. Usually delete the sentence.

allele.plain: one of the two copies of a gene

locus.plain: the place on a chromosome where a gene sits

in silico.plain: predicted by computer rather than measured in the laboratory

splice site.plain: the join between two parts of a gene's instructions

reanalysis.plain: looking again at the results they already have, using what has been learned since

secondary finding.plain: something the test found that was not what it was looking for
secondary finding.careful: Flag and route to genetic counselling. Do not explain the associated condition in the family half.

surveillance.plain: regular health checks that go with this finding
surveillance.careful: Not 'screening for disease'. Frame as standard care that catches things early, not as prediction.

always_keep.gene symbol: The family needs it to search, to find their community, and to say it at appointments. Keep it exactly as written and explain it once.
always_keep.syndrome name: Same reason — it is the word that finds other families.
always_keep.the name of the test: They will see it on letters and need to recognise it.
